title: 1 in 4 Americans Has a Second Job Nobody Pays Them For
description: 63 million Americans are caring for an aging parent or sick family member — and the hardest part isn't the caring. It's the paperwork. Source: AARP/National Alliance for Caregiving, Caregiving in the U.S. 2025. General information, not medical, legal, or financial advice.

scenes.narration: One in four adults in America is working a second job that nobody pays them for.

visual.post: a second job nobody pays for.

scenes.narration: Caring for an aging parent. A sick spouse. A family member who cannot manage alone anymore.

right.label: AFTER 5PM
right.text:
Mom's meds.
Dad's appointments.
No paycheck.

scenes.narration: Sixty three million Americans, according to A A R P. Twenty million more than just ten years ago.

visual.post: family caregivers. Up 20M in a decade.

scenes.narration: For one in four of them, the caring alone is a full time job. Forty plus hours. Every week.
Half of them take a financial hit for it — savings drained, hours cut, careers paused.

visual.post: suffer a financial impact from caregiving.

scenes.narration: And here is what caregivers will tell you. The hardest part is not the caring. They love the person.

visual.text:
The hardest part
isn't the caring.

scenes.narration: It is the pile. Discharge papers. Medication lists. Insurance letters. Appointment cards. And five family members texting — wait, what did the doctor say?

right.label: THE PILE
right.text:
Discharge papers.
Med lists.
Insurance letters.
"Wait — what did the doctor say?"

scenes.narration: If that pile is your life right now — you are not failing, and you are not alone. We are building something for exactly this. Follow along.

visual.title: The pile shouldn't be your second job. Follow along.
